citation: P. S. Ho, J. E. Lewis, H. S. Wildman and J. K. Howard, Auger study of preferred sputtering on binary alloy surfaces, Surface Science 57, 393–405 (1976)
source_access: Original article PDF supplied by the operator; only cited numerical facts transcribed. PDF and page images not redistributed.
terms: Facts, cited; original article copyright is not transferred to this repository.

tables.constant_from_source: All rows use 0.5 keV Ar+ (table footnote).
All rows use 38.4 at% Cu (table caption).

conditions.target: Homogeneous coevaporated Cu–Ni films on thermally grown SiO2; random grain orientation
conditions.incidence_source: Section 3, p. 398: about 70 degrees measured from the sample surface; converted to 20 degrees from normal.
conditions.temperature_note: Room temperature is stated for deposition, not irradiation.
conditions.ion_intensity_area_convention: Not resolved here; establish sample-area versus beam-normal-area convention before converting erosion to atoms/ion.
conditions.methods: Bulk composition: electron microprobe; ion intensity: Faraday cup; erosion: crater depth (Talystep and laser interferometry); AES: Cu 920 eV, corrected Ni 716 eV preferred.

columns.row_id: Local stable identifier; tN-rM means Table N, data row M (one-based).
columns.bulk_cu_at_percent: Cu atomic percent in the bulk alloy; Ni is the balance.
columns.energy_keV: Incident Ar+ ion energy in keV.
columns.ion_intensity_cm2_s: Reported ion intensity in ions per square centimetre per second.
columns.erosion_rate_angstrom_min: Measured sputter erosion rate in angstroms per minute; NOT atoms per ion.
columns.erosion_rate_reported_pm_angstrom_min: Printed plus/minus erosion-rate amount; crater-periphery deviations, not declared 1 sigma.
columns.r0_over_rinf: Authors’ ratio of extrapolated zero-time Cu/Ni AES signal ratio to equilibrium ratio; dimensionless, model/extrapolation dependent.
columns.r0_over_rinf_reported_pm: Printed plus/minus amount, mainly extrapolation uncertainty, not declared 1 sigma.
columns.tau_s: Authors’ fitted transient time constant in seconds; model dependent.
columns.tau_reported_pm_s: Printed plus/minus amount in seconds, mainly extrapolation uncertainty, not declared 1 sigma.

extraction.method: Table transcription from pdftotext, checked against rendered original pages. No figure digitization or simulation values.
extraction.second_read: 2026-10-19: all numeric cells and column units visually re-read on pp. 401–402 after initial text extraction; same assistant, not an independent reviewer.
extraction.corrections: None; conflicting source rows retained exactly.

limitations.reason: Same printed composition, energy, intensity and erosion rate, but inconsistent R0/Rinf and tau. Exclude this ambiguous pair from an initial benchmark until resolved; do not silently repair or merge.
At 0.5 keV AES may include material beneath the altered layer (discussion, pp. 403–404).
Initial surface oxide changes transient sputtering; R0 and tau depend on fitting oxide-cleared late-time data and extrapolating (pp. 399–402, 404).
Erosion rates average crater-periphery depths; spatial variation dominates their reported uncertainty. No covariance or statistical confidence level supplied (p. 404).

derived_composition.source_basis: Proportional AES calibration and oxide-cleared R0 extrapolation, pp. 400–402. Our algebra, not a printed composition column.
derived_composition.limitations: Requires valid proportional calibration and representative AES sampling; propagate bulk-composition and extrapolation uncertainties.
